newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares ease at open, no sharp fall seen.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares ease at open, no sharp fall seen.

text.p: Leading Russian shares eased in early trade on Thursday on continued profit taking traders said, predicting the correction would be slight and would not last for more than a week.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index opened at 432.86, slightly off Wednesday's record 433.12 closing on a record $96.3 million record turnover.

"The market is correcting, thank goodness -- people had to change their minds and stop buying at any price, " said senior Creditanstalt-Grant trader Andrei Galperin, adding the market would sink no more than five percent in the next week.
"I don't think one should expect a crash -- it will be an uneven movement: one step up, one step down. There's still a lot of money on the market."
National power utility UES EESR.RTS slipped to $0.3530 at 0830 GMT from 0.$3640 at the close on Wednesday.
Shares in Russia's biggest oil company LUKoil LKOH.RTS eased to $19.75 from $20.35, and oil company Surgutneftegaz SNGS.RTS dipped to $1.09 from $1.14.
Renaissance Capital trader Vladimir Chkikvadze said unsatisified demand on individual stocks was supporting prices in some shares after a homogenous downward trend after the open.
"Yesterday we saw the most significant rise in prices on the highest volumes...Now the market is nervous and the question is whether buyers will turn up on a falling market," he said.
"A continuation of the correction is very likely but one shouldn't expect a plunge."
